Name: Chrystal Pratt
Badge: Reading to Write: They Say / I Say
Which version of the They Say / I Say routine (with visual texts or with annotation) feels like the best fit for your students right now? Why?:

Visual texts are the most beneficial right now because my students need very concrete visuals when trying to respond with writing. They really struggle with coming up with their own ideas and so having something to have their brains trained on initially really stirred up some though provoking writing.

Describe one way you might adapt the They Say / I Say framework to align with the types of texts your students read most often (e.g., articles, visuals, multimodal texts).:

I actually use this a lot for classroom discussions when I want to start the students on their own path of thinking instead of going along with the crowd. I start with "You know they say...." and before I know it there is a whole classroom discussion going on about different opinions ion the given topic.

What, if anything, do you need help thinking through as you plan for using They Say / I Say in your classroom?:

I really think I have a good grasp on using this as a regular thought provoking/writing invoking project in my room.
